clue.text: Dickens character having to study clue for young wimp

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn by heart
a key is a clue to a puzzle
a chick is a young bird
a weed is a feeble, weak person

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure reads up on a clue to describe a feeble youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: Four pieces in a row give CONKEY CHICKWEED; 'young' stands for its offspring noun, as in a young bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Conkey Chickweed is a burglar mentioned in Oliver Twist, so he is one of the novelist's creations.

clue.text: Dickens character — just one for Crompton and then some more

parts.note: Richmal Crompton wrote the Just William books about a single boy
more than one of the same boy, in the plural

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure is compared with a children's author's hero, plus a few extra.
explanation.walkthrough: Richmal Crompton's schoolboy hero stars in the Just William stories; take one of him, then several, to get WILLIAM WILLIAMS.
explanation.definitionFit: William Williams is a minor figure in Our Mutual Friend, one of the novelist's books.

clue.text: Blunders involving Conservatives, say, raised hidden dangers

indicators.note: to involve something is to take it inside, so the blunders wrap around the next piece

parts.note: boobs are silly mistakes

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word means reading it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: the Conservatives are an example of a political party

explanation.surface: Political gaffes by Tories turn out to be concealed perils.
explanation.walkthrough: The Conservatives are a British political party; 'say' marks them as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Booby traps are concealed devices set to injure or surprise anyone who triggers them unawares.

clue.text: Dry rot in building endlessly retaining water

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits in the middle of the building
without its end, the final letter of the building is dropped

parts.note: a house is a building

indicators.note: rot means the preceding word has decayed and fallen apart into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Dry rot in a building that holds water, which sounds like a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry rot' looks like one fungal phrase, but rot is the anagram signal working on Dry alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Hydrous is the chemistry term for a substance containing water, often chemically bound within it.

clue.text: The post in a pickle, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as said out loud, so the word is chosen by its sound

parts.note: a pickle is a jam, a tight spot

explanation.surface: The mail is in a mess, according to reports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The post' suggests letters, but it is an upright of a door frame.
explanation.definitionFit: A jamb is the vertical side piece of a doorway or window frame, an upright support.

clue.text: Dickens character, one stoned by taste and smell

parts.note: a cherry is a fruit with a stone in it
to peck at food is to taste a little of it
a sniff is a smell

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure is pelted with stones, then sampled and sniffed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoned' suggests a victim of stoning or drugs, but it means having a stone, as fruit does.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherry Pecksniff is a daughter of the hypocrite Seth Pecksniff in Martin Chuzzlewit.

clue.text: Dickens character cooking a lean, thin shellfish

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
a winkle is a small edible sea snail

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure prepares a skinny seafood dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Nathaniel Winkle is the hapless sporting member of the club in The Pickwick Papers.

clue.text: I'm no dreadful politician offering warning

indicators.note: something dreadful is in a terrible state, so the preceding letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
a Tory is a British Conservative politician

explanation.surface: A self-deprecating Tory issues a caution while denying he is awful.
explanation.definitionFit: Monitory is an adjective meaning cautionary, giving admonition or advice about danger.

clue.text: Religious retreat remains for sheep

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A spiritual retreat keeps the leftovers for the flock.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community where people go for spiritual instruction.

clue.text: Space station stops short, having turned round about a year

indicators.note: turned round means the whole thing is read back to front
about means going round, so the stopping word wraps around the year

parts.note: to balk is to stop short and refuse to go on
Y is the abbreviation for year

explanation.surface: A space station halts abruptly and turns around after a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like a shortening signal, but 'stops short' is one phrase meaning balks.
explanation.definitionFit: Skylab was the first American orbiting laboratory, launched in 1973 and occupied by astronauts.

clue.text: With which people will come back into a particular society?

definitions.text: With which people will come back into a particular society?

parts.words: With which people will come back into a particular society?
parts.note: surface reading: the means of being readmitted to some club
setter's reading: being born again into the world, as in reincarnation

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like rejoining a club, but the society is the living world and people return by being born anew.
explanation.definitionFit: Reincarnation means a soul is born again into a new life, returning to human society.

clue.text: Paul, but not me, gets the bird

indicators.note: but not asks for one word with another taken away from it

parts.note: Paul is the setter, so from his point of view the word is what he is called
taken as written

explanation.surface: Paul is jeered at, though the speaker escapes it.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter of this puzzle is Paul, so Paul is the setter's own name; remove ME from it. 'Gets the bird' hints at being booed.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling of Asia, famous for mimicking human speech.

clue.text: Complicated rune required in playing knightly pursuit

indicators.note: in places the mixed letters inside the word for playing

parts.note: toying is playing idly

indicators.note: complicated means tangled up, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: An intricate magic letter is needed in a game of chivalry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tourneying is taking part in a tournament, jousting on horseback as medieval knights did.

clue.text: Virgin spirit with two large islands

parts.note: virgin means new and untouched
zeal is spirit or fervour
and means along with

explanation.surface: A fresh soul accompanies a pair of big landmasses.
explanation.definitionFit: The country consists chiefly of the North Island and the South Island in the Pacific.

clue.text: Possibly Barnum won with sham performance?

indicators.note: a performance puts on a show, so the letters are acted out in a new order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging
taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: The great circus promoter succeeded with a fake act.
explanation.walkthrough: P. T. Barnum, the American circus impresario, was famous for hoaxes, so a sham performance fits him well.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnum is an example of an impresario of spectacle, hence the 'Possibly' marking an example.

clue.text: One cleans up proverbial losers, end first

indicators.note: the final letter is taken from the back and put at the front

parts.note: from the saying finders keepers, losers weepers

explanation.surface: Someone tidies up after the beaten, putting the end at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: The playground saying runs 'finders keepers, losers weepers'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweeper brushes floors or streets clean, a person or machine that tidies rubbish away.

clue.text: Novelist reportedly willing to provide an exercise in action

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the novelist's name is taken by its sound

parts.note: Evelyn Waugh, the English novelist, whose name is pronounced like this
to be game is to be willing

explanation.surface: A writer is said to be happy to offer a practical training session.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech Waugh and war sound the same, as the r is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: A war game is a military exercise simulating battle, a rehearsal of combat operations.

clue.text: Fare from Manchester consists of half an OT book, plus cover

indicators.note: half means only the first six of its twelve letters are kept

parts.note: a book of the Old Testament
to cake is to coat or cover thickly

explanation.surface: A Manchester food is described as a Bible book plus a lid.
explanation.walkthrough: Eccles is a town in Greater Manchester, home of this pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eccles cake is a flaky pastry filled with currants, named after the town near Manchester.

clue.text: 14 bird demanding fruit

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the flightless national bird of the country at 14
second meaning: the furry green fruit

explanation.surface: A bird from the antipodes insists on being fed fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the flightless New Zealand bird and the green fruit originally sold under that name.

clue.text: Prepared to see a joker imbibing one can

indicators.note: to imbibe is to drink in, so the joker takes the next pieces inside

parts.note: taken as written
a wag is a jokey person
I is the Roman numeral one
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: Someone is ready to watch a comedian down a single tin of drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Awaiting means expecting or being ready for something about to arrive or appear.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about working? Not I!

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written, for rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are keen on their job flatly refuses.
explanation.definitionFit: Being into something is an informal idiom for being keen on or interested in it.

clue.text: Heather purchases fashionable piece of material

indicators.note: to purchase is to take hold of, so the heather holds the next piece

parts.note: ling is a common heather
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather buys a trendy bit of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A lining is a layer of fabric sewn inside a garment, curtain or bag.

clue.text: Woman's with German person alone

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
mit is the German word for with

explanation.surface: A woman is accompanied by a German, so someone else is left by themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A hermit lives in solitude, deliberately withdrawn from society and other people.

clue.text: Diversified engine part

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the pipe assembly carrying gases to or from cylinders

explanation.definitionFit: The word means having many forms, and also names the branched pipe on an engine's cylinders.
